correctness.rationale: The four reference gradients are explicit polynomials; exact integration gives all six edge weights in the proof. Since every Bernoulli and edge diffusion factor is strictly positive, a negative weight makes an off-diagonal of the central cell of any 3x3 tiling positive and cannot be cancelled by same-shape adjacent cells. Nonnegative weights give zero-column-sum Z-matrix edge blocks; the strictly positive-weight graph is connected even when a bound is attained, giving an irreducibly diagonally dominant Dirichlet M-matrix. The two geometric inequalities are equivalent to the six weight signs. Eigenvalue algebra yields the exact maximum kappa_2(J)=(3+sqrt(5))/2, with an explicit extremizer. Symbolic matrix reconstruction and 2233 supplementary finite assertions pass from check.py. Limits: no assertion for general quadrilateral meshes, inverse positivity outside M-matrix class, or convergence orders.

value.rationale: This identifies a motivated complete geometry criterion for the simplest genuinely nonsimplicial mesh of the recently proposed complete-graph IBEAM scheme. In practice it replaces an abstract local weight-sign assumption by exact tests on element lengths and shear, valid at arbitrary Péclet number, and proves a sharp golden-ratio-squared Jacobian distortion barrier with a realizable extremizer. This gives a robust mesh-design filter (and shows a scalar condition number alone is insufficient), rather than an arbitrary small numerical example or a merely substituted parameter. It does not imply convergence rates or guarantee non-monotonicity outside the M-matrix class.
